name: rusty_alloc
baseline: mimalloc v2.4.5 (also jemalloc, glibc malloc, dlmalloc on wasm32, esp-alloc on ESP32-S3)
workload: Callgrind instruction counts (allocator-only and whole-program) on lua, perl and sqlite under LD_PRELOAD on x86-64 Linux; plus wasm32 churn and ESP32-S3 throughput.
claimed_speedup: Allocator-only instructions 0.52x / 0.81x / 0.83x of mimalloc on lua / perl / sqlite; whole program 0.96 / 0.99 / 1.00 vs mimalloc and 0.84 / 0.89 / 0.98 vs jemalloc; wasm32 churn 4.9-7.3x faster than dlmalloc; ESP32-S3 2.1-3.9x faster than esp-alloc
hardware: x86-64 Linux (CPU model not stated); XIAO ESP32-S3 at 240 MHz
tradeoffs: Rebuild of the mimalloc architecture in safe-leaning Rust; freed memory stays committed by default like mimalloc; ESP32 build needs a 64 KiB RAM floor and returned 357 NULLs in a 50,000-allocation hostile churn test; refuses 64 KiB-aligned requests.
caveats: First-party only. Instruction counts, not wall time; whole-program lead over mimalloc is under 5% and sqlite is 1.00. CPU model and compiler flags not stated; lua count is not repeatable (about 0.26% drift). Very new repo with few stars. Read from the README only; bench scripts (bench/icount-arms.sh) not run.
found_via: WebSearch: rusty_alloc pure-Rust rebuild of mimalloc instructions benchmark github

name: fc_malloc
workload: Random producer-consumer test: one array per thread of 500K slots, random 128-byte allocs and frees, single thread and 10 threads.
claimed_speedup: Single thread 2.6s vs glibc 5.8s and jemalloc 4.5s; 10 threads 6.8s vs glibc 18.2s and jemalloc 13.6s
tradeoffs: Dedicated thread moves freed blocks to the shared pool, so it costs a core; each thread maps 4 MB chunks, so memory use is high; 128-byte test only.
caveats: Author calls these initial benchmarks. Compiler, flags, CPU and jemalloc version not stated. No license file found (README gives none), so code cannot be copied. Last commit 2013.
found_via: WebSearch: github malloc replacement faster than glibc malloc multithreaded allocator lock-free README benchmarks

name: rlsf
workload: Alloc/dealloc latency on an STM32F401 microcontroller and code size on WebAssembly, measured with FarCri.rs.
claimed_speedup: rlsf 260-320 cycles vs dlmalloc 450-750 cycles (buddy-alloc 340-440, umm_malloc 300-700); WebAssembly code size 1267 bytes vs dlmalloc 9613 bytes
tradeoffs: Constant-time two-level segregated fit for no_std and real-time use; no thread scaling; embedded niche, not a hosted malloc replacement.
caveats: Numbers appear only as image alt text on the README. Baseline dlmalloc is not in the list, and no comparison to malloc, jemalloc or mimalloc. Flags not stated. Search-time snippet of the README footnotes not opened.

name: Talc
baseline: DLmalloc (Rust wasm default), RLSF, Galloc, FRuSA, system allocator
workload: Random alloc/dealloc/realloc actions (single and multi-threaded), heap efficiency and microbench via benches/src; wasm size and speed.
claimed_speedup: No numbers in text; README: 'DLmalloc and RLSF's GlobalTlsf are worse in both size and performance to Talc' (plots only)
tradeoffs: no_std and WebAssembly allocator. Linked-list dlmalloc-style design; author says jemalloc and mimalloc are better on hosted systems and Talc scales worse under contention.
caveats: Results are plots only. The author states Talc is slower than FRuSA under concurrency and that System, jemalloc and mimalloc are not compared. Benchmark code is public but compiler, flags and CPU are missing. Does not beat any baseline in the list.
found_via: WebSearch: talc allocator Rust faster than dlmalloc benchmark github

name: XenoAtom.Allocators (TLSF)
baseline: C runtime malloc/free (MSVC CRT on Windows)
workload: 2048 allocations and frees of random sizes 64-4096 bytes, BenchmarkDotNet, .NET 8.0.6.
claimed_speedup: Tlsf 82.27 us vs Libc 105.34 us (ratio 0.78), '20%+ faster'
tradeoffs: Managed .NET allocator managing a caller-provided region (not a drop-in malloc); single-threaded; the libc call goes through interop.
caveats: Tiny single-size-mix benchmark; baseline path includes P/Invoke-style overhead; Windows MSVC CRT only. Benchmark code is in src/XenoAtom.Allocators.Bench but was not opened.

name: jdz_allocator
baseline: C malloc (glibc via Zig c_allocator), Zig GeneralPurposeAllocator, rpmalloc Zig port, zimalloc
workload: mimalloc-bench suite via LD_PRELOAD, plus 75,000,000 linearly distributed 1-80000 byte allocations per thread without cross-thread frees.
claimed_speedup: No numbers in text: charts only; README says global allocator matches rpmalloc 'within the margin of error' with less memory; default config 'significantly slower than rpmalloc at high contention'
tradeoffs: Zig-only API plus LD_PRELOAD shared libraries; global variant needs deinitThread calls; page sizes above 64 KiB unsupported; high RSS on xmalloc-test.
caveats: Charts are images on imgur; text gives no speedup versus malloc or jemalloc, and does not claim to beat mimalloc. Author calls the Zig benchmark unrealistic and the allocator not battle-tested. Weak qualifier.
